chapter_title: Concerning the Purification of these Four Elements [that have been place]d in the Flesh.
chapter_note: The chapter is predominantly old, systematic correspondential teaching about the four light-elements’ mixture, purification in the body, and the resulting emissions (triadic chains). It is wrapped in a brief hagiographic opening (¶1) and ends with an institutional/application paragraph about the elect vs. sinners (¶9), which crosses from cosmic mechanism to church categories.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic scene-setting (“Once again… the apostle… among the congregation”), a compilation frame marker; no cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The four elements [are what is] purified. From the beginning they are holy ones, living ones, and enlighteners. However, when they undertood [ ... ] in that first struggle, the waste was [mixed] in with them, and the Darkness of the enemy was mixed with them. And when they were come into the body, stripping off these polluted garments, they set them in the flesh. Their pollutions, which they have stripped off, shall be displayed in a [ ... ] and become a danger to the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal mechanism of mixture/purification (cosmic event → bodily process) without citation or institutional address; “first struggle” + elements as ‘holy/living/enlighteners’ is characteristic systematic cosmology.

paragraphs.core_text: The discharge of this pollution, that [the fir]e shall disgorge and place in the body, is [blo]od. The discharge of the blood is anger. The discharge of anger is the humours.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic substrate-style correspondential chain (element → bodily substance → affect → physiological state) in a tight, iterative structure.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.240⟩
Also, the emissions that the waters discharge from them are lust. The discharge of lust is bitterness. The emission of bitterness is f[e]ver.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic triadic emissions chain; no audience address or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The emission that light shall disgorge is flesh. The emission of flesh is gloom. [The] emission of gloom is obstinacy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Same iterative correspondential mechanism (element → body/affect/mental state). The vocabulary remains within the system’s internal psychophysiology rather than polemic or discipline.

paragraphs.core_text: The emissions that the tree shall disgorge, they are the voices of the winds of shame. The emission of winds of shame [is ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary/corrupt, but still presented as an emissions-mapping in the same formal series; “tree” likely reflects an internal technical term (perhaps for wind) rather than institutional reference.

paragraphs.core_text: The emission of the [tear] is the [ ... ] of these twelve emissions.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Though lacunose, it continues the enumerative/structural exposition (“these twelve emissions”), consistent with a pre-compilation schematic list.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] these four elements shall [ ... ] what are gathered in are [f]ound by the management of this soul food [that] enters the body. When they enter the body, they are cleansed and purified and established [i]n their living image, which is the new man. They shall live [ ... ] and receive the Light Mind and be purified in their image; and they come forth, being cleansed and holy. They attain their first rest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Process-description of purification through ‘soul food’ and restoration to ‘living image’; still cosmological/anthropological mechanism (how purification works), not a Gospel/NT citation and not an ecclesial rule.

Crosses into institutional categorization (“the elect”, “the sinners”) and applies the mechanism to community sorting (elect vs. sinners), with a moralizing consequence statement (sins → transmigration). This is cosmos→church/world application rather than the older cosmos→cosmos mapping.
